name: messages
title: Cards and messages
summary: Makes greeting cards and short letters in the resident's own words, ready to print and saved on their laptop.
instructions: Their words, never yours. Help only if asked, in their voice, adding no feeling. Read it back. Changes by voice. Unclear who: ask aloud. Never describe the screen. Card: show_fronts, pick_front, set_words. Note: plain_message. send_it when they want it sent or seem done. Never say it went unless told. Silent during the count. Spell addresses, never read them. Never write anyone unasked.

actions.name: show_fronts
actions.description: Start a card: shows three or four numbered fronts for who it's for and the occasion. The result lists number and name.

person.description: Who it's for, as they said it

occasion.description: The occasion, birthday if not said

likes.description: Words about what that person loves

line.description: A short personal line for the front, such as for my son

actions.name: pick_front
actions.description: Choose a front by number, name or a word about it, like the second one or the one with the lake.

actions.name: set_words
actions.description: Put their words on the card as said, and any later change. Saves it. The result has read_back to read aloud.

signature.description: How they sign it, in their words

actions.name: set_hand
actions.description: Change the handwriting, plain or cursive. With no choice it swaps. It's remembered for next time.

actions.name: change_verse
actions.description: Change the printed verse to the next one that suits the card, or take it off.

actions.name: change_front
actions.description: Go back to the fronts for the same person and occasion. Their words are kept.

actions.name: read_back
actions.description: Get the verse, words and signature, to read aloud.

actions.name: save_card_now
actions.description: Say whether it's saved. Each change already saves it, so this only tells them so, with the date.

actions.name: print_card
actions.description: Print what's on screen. The result says how it prints and folds, and that mailing needs facility help.

actions.name: send_it
actions.description: When they want it sent, or you think they're done. Shows the last look and gives you the line to say. It can't send: the app hears their yes itself.

person.description: Only when they just told you who it's for

actions.name: give_address
actions.description: An email address they said aloud. Read spelled back letter by letter, ask if that's right, then call address_right.

address.description: As they said it, like mark dot hollis at gmail dot com

person.description: Whose address it is, if they said

actions.name: address_right
actions.description: Their answer after you spelled the address back: true if it's right.

right.description: true if they said it's right

actions.name: keep_address
actions.description: Their answer when you asked about keeping the address for next time: true to keep it.

keep.description: true if they want it kept

actions.name: save_contact
actions.description: Remember someone they write to. Never for an email address: give_address handles those.

actions.name: find_contact
actions.description: Whether you know this person: relationship, and whether an email is saved. Never the address itself.

name.description: A name, first name or relationship

actions.name: plain_message
actions.description: A plain message on cream paper, no card. Also for any change to it. Written as them, in their words.

actions.name: show_keepsake
actions.description: Show a keepsake page for someone's date. The weekday is worked out from the next such date.

age_line.description: A short age line, like Fifty-two this year

memory_line.description: Only what they told you about this person

who.description: Which of you is showing it

actions.name: open_saved
actions.description: Bring back the latest saved card or message for a person, or the latest of all.

actions.name: close
actions.description: Put the card away and go back to Mary. It stays saved.
